note: The cast: named characters whose voices are made by the cast recipe (ADR-0060, SND-018; Tools/voice/cast/make_cast_voices.py). A profile states gender ('voice_is'), age and accent, and its 'description' opens with them: a voice model settles whatever is left open by chance. 'card' is the one clip the owner approved as the person's voice; it and the mood cards beside it are kept and never made again. Only the owner approves a card, by ear, in chat. Change a description only with the owner, then make and show a new card.

recipe.note: The same for everyone. Nothing here is per line and nothing is chosen by ear (owner, 2026-11-26).
recipe.card_text: I was down at the market this morning, before the tram came through. There was bread on every stall, and the whole square smelled of it.
recipe.card_direction: Speaking in their ordinary voice, plainly and steadily, at a natural conversational pace, with no strong emotion.

mood_text.happy: Oh, that's wonderful news! I couldn't be happier, truly. Come in, come in, this calls for something special!
mood_text.sad: I'm sorry. I thought I had more time with her. It's very quiet in the house now, and I don't know what to do with the quiet.
mood_text.angry: No. I told you once, and I will not tell you again. Get out of my sight, and do not come back here.
mood_text.surprised: What? No, that can't be right! You're telling me it was here the whole time? I don't believe it!
mood_text.thinking: Hmm. Let me think about that. It might work, if we're careful, though I'm not sure. Give me a moment.

length_check.note: A clip's length against its words, to flag a fault without listening (owner, 2026-11-26: 'track the size of the clip as an indicator and flag it'). A clip longer than words / slowest_words_a_second + grace_seconds has more in it than the line (the description read aloud, a runaway that never stopped: Noor's morning/report 18.3 s for 5 words, verdict/v_lie 73 s for 28); shorter than words / fastest_words_a_second, words are missing. Measured on Noor's 35 Maya1 clips: the good ones 1.3 to 2.8 words a second, her card 2.8. A flagged clip is not used; it is voiced again as it is.

people.trade: Master baker, owner of the Stone Oven
people.how_they_talk: Short sentences. Never two words where one will do. Compliments so dry you notice them an hour later. Counts everything: change, loaves, people. She says very little, until the one night at the crock when she says it all.
people.description: A 58-year-old woman with a British accent, a master baker who has opened her shop at four every morning for thirty-four years. Her voice is low for a woman, dry and a little worn with age. She is economical and unhurried: short sentences, no warmth wasted, firm but never loud.

people.trade: Owner of Crumb & Co, Eastgate Mall
people.how_they_talk: Fast, warm, always selling something, mostly himself. Jokes to keep the talk off the one subject. Goes quiet exactly once per scene, and that line is the true one.
people.description: A 49-year-old man with a British accent, the owner of a bakery counter in a shopping mall. A bright, warm, quick salesman's voice in a middle pitch, charming and always performing, a born showman.

people.trade: Bakery assistant at the Stone Oven; pastry
people.how_they_talk: Talks in first drafts. Blurts the thing everyone else was carefully not saying, then apologises to the room in general. More honest when something is on fire.
people.description: A 19-year-old bakery apprentice with a British accent and a young woman's light, bright voice. Earnest, quick and a little nervous, the words tumble out before they are ready.

people.card_text: It's called “Proved”. There's a key change where the dough knocks back. It's the first one I've ever sung with my eyes open.
people.card_note: This card is a clip the owner approved, not made from the description: it cannot be made again, so keep the file.

people.trade: Miller of the last stone mill in the valley
people.how_they_talk: Slow and exact, with pauses that aren't empty. Talks about machines as if they were livestock and about people as if they were weather.
people.description: A 61-year-old woman with a rural British accent, a miller who has worked the last stone mill in the valley all her life. A low, weathered, steady woman's voice, clearly a woman. Slow and exact, with thoughtful pauses, plain and unsentimental.

people.trade: Grower of Old Wall Red; retired in name only
people.how_they_talk: Biblical cadence. Gets quieter as he gets more certain. Calls the wheat “she”.
people.description: A 74-year-old man with a rural British accent, a farmer who has grown wheat all his life. An old man's voice: thin, dry and a little cracked with age, low and quiet. He speaks slowly with a solemn, almost biblical rhythm, and gets quieter as he gets more certain.
